dashboard.how_are_you: How are you today? Your wellbeing matters.
dashboard.no_programs: You haven't started any programs yet
dashboard.tip_text: Spending 2 minutes a day on your emotional wellbeing can change your entire week.

tips.0: Sundays are perfect for planning your emotional week. What do you need to prioritize this week to feel good?
tips.1: Start Monday with intention: write one word that captures how you want to feel today and return to it if you lose track.
tips.2: Midweek, take a 2-minute pause. Breathe deeply 4 times and ask yourself: how am I really doing?
tips.3: Connecting with someone from your home country can recharge your emotional energy. Who can you message today?
tips.4: Thursdays are perfect for celebrating small wins. What have you achieved this week that deserves recognition?
tips.5: Before the weekend, release tension: shake your arms, stretch your neck, and let go of what doesn't serve you.
tips.6: On Saturdays, explore something new in your city. Discovering a different spot can renew your sense of belonging.

emergency.subtitle: Quick tools for difficult moments
emergency.completed_msg: You've completed the exercise. Remember that taking care of your wellbeing is an act of courage.

exercises.box_desc: 4-4-4-4 breathing technique to calm the nervous system
box_steps: Hold your lungs empty counting to 4
exercises.grounding_desc: Sensory grounding to return to the present
grounding_steps: Name 5 things you can SEE around you
reframe_steps: Identify the thought that bothers you
Is there a more balanced way to see it?
What would you tell a friend in this situation?
Write your new, more balanced thought
exercises.body_desc: Mindfulness to release physical and emotional tension
body_steps: Close your eyes and take 3 deep breaths
Bring your attention to the top of your head
Slowly move down: forehead, eyes, jaw... notice tensions
Continue through neck, shoulders, arms, hands
Breathe and release any tension you've found
compassion_steps: Acknowledge: 'This is a moment of suffering'
Normalize: 'Adapting to another country is hard. I'm not alone in this'
Place your hand on your heart and say: 'I give myself the care I need'
Ask yourself: 'What do I need right now?'
Commit to giving yourself what you need
exercises.478_desc: Deep relaxation technique for anxious moments
478_steps: Inhale through your nose counting to 4
Exhale through your mouth counting to 8

resources.title: Resources 🌿
resources.subtitle: You don't have to do this alone. Here are real resources for expats in the Netherlands.
resources.helplines_subtitle: If you need to talk to someone right now
resources.helplines_113_desc: Suicide prevention line in the Netherlands. 24/7, free and confidential.
resources.helplines_luisterlijn_desc: Anonymous listening line. You can call, chat or email. Available in Dutch and English.
resources.helplines_crisis_desc: Crisis support in multiple languages, including Spanish and English.
resources.community_subtitle: Connect with people who understand what you're going through
resources.community_internations_desc: Global expat network with events, activities and local groups in all Dutch cities.
resources.community_meetup_desc: Meetup groups for expats: sports, languages, networking, emotional support and more.
resources.community_reddit_desc: Active Reddit community where expats share experiences, advice and support.
resources.health_subtitle: How to access psychology and psychiatry in the Netherlands
resources.health_gp_desc: In the Netherlands you need a registered GP (huisarts). They are the gateway to mental healthcare: book an appointment and explain you need psychological or psychiatric support. Your basic insurance (basisverzekering) covers mental health with a referral.
resources.health_referral_desc: Your GP assesses your situation and refers you to Basis GGZ (mild-moderate issues) or Specialistische GGZ (complex issues, psychiatry). Without the verwijsbrief, insurance won't cover therapy. Advocate for yourself if you feel you need it.
resources.health_wait_desc: Waiting times for psychology and psychiatry can be 3 to 12 months in NL. Check wachttijden.ggz.nl to compare times by area and provider. In the meantime, OpenUp, your GP or the POH-GGZ (mental health assistant at your practice) can offer initial support.
resources.therapists_subtitle: Professionals who speak your language and understand your situation
resources.therapists_igp_desc: Network of international GPs who can refer you to psychologists in English/Spanish.
resources.therapists_openup_desc: Free online mental wellness sessions in English. Many Dutch employers cover it.
resources.therapists_psychtoday_desc: Therapist directory in the Netherlands. Filter by language, specialty and insurance type.

flashcards.title: How are you feeling? Pick a card ✨
flashcards.complete_msg: You've gone through all the cards. Remember: every emotion is valid and temporary.
flashcards.ansiedad_msg: It's normal to feel anxious when adapting to a new country. Your body is on alert because everything is new.
flashcards.ansiedad_s1: Cross your arms over your chest, hands on opposite shoulders.
flashcards.ansiedad_s2: Close your eyes and breathe slowly.
flashcards.ansiedad_s4: Continue for 2 minutes at the rhythm of your breathing.
flashcards.ansiedad_s5: Notice how your body starts to relax.
flashcards.tristeza_msg: Nostalgia is the price of the love you feel for your home. Missing it isn't weakness.
flashcards.tristeza_s1: Write 3 things you miss from home.
flashcards.tristeza_s2: Now write 3 new things you've discovered here.
flashcards.tristeza_s4: Allow yourself to feel gratitude for both realities.
flashcards.fomo_msg: You're also living moments others would envy. You just take them for granted.
flashcards.fomo_s1: Look around: where are you right now?
flashcards.fomo_s2: Take a mental photo of this moment.
flashcards.fomo_s4: Repeat: 'I'm exactly where I need to be.'
flashcards.soledad_msg: Expat loneliness is real: you're surrounded by people but no one truly knows you.
flashcards.soledad_s1: Think of someone you've had a nice conversation with.
flashcards.soledad_s2: Send them a message: 'Hey! How are you?'
flashcards.soledad_s3: If you don't have anyone, look for a local event this week.
flashcards.soledad_s4: One genuine connection can change everything.
flashcards.impostor_msg: You're not a fraud. You're learning an entire world from scratch.
flashcards.impostor_s1: Write 5 hard things you've achieved since arriving.
flashcards.impostor_s2: Include 'small' things: seeing a doctor in another language, doing paperwork…
flashcards.impostor_s3: Say out loud: 'I did all of this.'
flashcards.impostor_s4: Add a new achievement every week.
flashcards.choque_msg: Your brain is processing thousands of new rules at once. It's normal to feel lost.
flashcards.choque_s1: Write something that surprised you today about the local culture.
flashcards.choque_s2: Ask yourself: 'Why does this bother me?'
flashcards.choque_s3: Look for the positive side behind that custom.
flashcards.choque_s4: Understanding doesn't mean accepting everything, but it gives you peace.

legal.terms_s2_text: Rooted Abroad provides digital tools for emotional wellbeing support, including journaling, self-assessment questionnaires, guided exercises, and educational content. These tools are designed for self-help and personal development purposes. They are NOT a substitute for professional psychological, psychiatric, or medical care.

legal.privacy_s1_text: The data controller for your personal data is Rooted Abroad, operating from the Netherlands under the Algemene Verordening Gegevensbescherming (AVG/GDPR).
legal.privacy_s2_text: We collect: email address and name (upon registration), emotional journal entries (mood, emotion, free text), self-assessment results (scores and answers), and program progress. This data may include special category data (health) under GDPR Art. 9.

legal.privacy_s6_text: We use encryption in transit (TLS/SSL), restricted database access through row-level security (RLS) policies, and secure storage within the European Union.
legal.privacy_s7_text: To exercise your rights or for privacy questions, contact us at: privacy@expatrooted.com
